The interpretation of His saying, exalted be His praise and sanctified be His names: ﴿The Striking Calamity! What is the Striking Calamity? And what will make you know what the Striking Calamity is? It is a Day when mankind will be like scattered moths, and the mountains will be like tufts of carded wool. As for him whose scales are heavy, he will be in a pleasing life. And as for him whose scales are light, his mother will be the Abyss. And what will make you know what it is? A Fire blazing fiercely.﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿al-Qari'ah﴾ (the Striking Calamity) is the Hour by which the hearts of people are struck with its terror, and by the great affliction that will befall them then; it is a morning after which there is no night.

Ahl al-ta'wil (the people of interpretation) said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿al-Qari'ah﴾: it is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection, which Allah has magnified and warned His servants against.

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿The Striking Calamity, what is the Striking Calamity﴾ he said: it is the Hour.

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: ﴿The Striking Calamity, what is the Striking Calamity﴾ he said: it is the Hour.

* Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, saying: I heard that al-Qari'ah, al-Waqi'ah and al-Haqqah are the Resurrection.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿What is the Striking Calamity?﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, is magnifying the matter of the Resurrection and the Hour by which the servants are struck with its terror: What is the Striking Calamity? It means: What is the Hour by which creation is struck with its terror? That is, how great it is, how dreadful, and how terrifying.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And what will make you know what the Striking Calamity is?﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): And what will make you aware, O Muhammad, of what the Striking Calamity is?

* *

As for His saying: ﴿It is a Day when mankind will be like scattered moths﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: The Striking Calamity is a Day when mankind will be like moths, which fling themselves into the fire and the lamp, being neither gnats nor flies. By "scattered" (al-mabthuth) is meant "dispersed."

Ahl al-ta'wil said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿a Day when mankind will be like scattered moths﴾: this is the moth which you have seen rushing headlong into the fire.

* Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿a Day when mankind will be like scattered moths﴾: this is a simile which Allah has made. Ahl al-ta'wil said the same as what we have said about this.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And what will make you know what it is?﴾

The interpretation of His saying, exalted be His praise and sanctified be His names: ﴿The Striking Calamity! What is the Striking Calamity? And what will make you know what the Striking Calamity is? It is a Day when mankind will be like scattered moths, and the mountains will be like tufts of carded wool. As for him whose scales are heavy, he will be in a pleasing life. And as for him whose scales are light, his mother will be the Abyss. And what will make you know what it is? A Fire blazing fiercely.﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿al-Qari'ah﴾ (the Striking Calamity) is the Hour by which the hearts of people are struck with its terror, and by the great affliction that will befall them then; it is a morning after which there is no night.

Ahl al-ta'wil (the people of interpretation) said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿al-Qari'ah﴾: it is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection, which Allah has magnified and warned His servants against.

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿The Striking Calamity, what is the Striking Calamity﴾ he said: it is the Hour.

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: ﴿The Striking Calamity, what is the Striking Calamity﴾ he said: it is the Hour.

* Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, saying: I heard that al-Qari'ah, al-Waqi'ah and al-Haqqah are the Resurrection.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿What is the Striking Calamity?﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, is magnifying the matter of the Resurrection and the Hour by which the servants are struck with its terror: What is the Striking Calamity? It means: What is the Hour by which creation is struck with its terror? That is, how great it is, how dreadful, and how terrifying.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And what will make you know what the Striking Calamity is?﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): And what will make you aware, O Muhammad, of what the Striking Calamity is?

* *

As for His saying: ﴿It is a Day when mankind will be like scattered moths﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: The Striking Calamity is a Day when mankind will be like moths, which fling themselves into the fire and the lamp, being neither gnats nor flies. By "scattered" (al-mabthuth) is meant "dispersed."

Ahl al-ta'wil said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿a Day when mankind will be like scattered moths﴾: this is the moth which you have seen rushing headlong into the fire.

* Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿a Day when mankind will be like scattered moths﴾: this is a simile which Allah has made. Some of the Arabic grammarians used to say: its meaning is like the swarming of locusts, one riding upon another; so it will be with people that day, some surging over others.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And the mountains will be like tufts of carded wool﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: and on the Day when the mountains will be like carded wool. Al-'ihn (wool) is the various colours of wool.

Ahl al-ta'wil said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: ﴿And the mountains will be like tufts of carded wool﴾: he said: carded wool.

* Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: it is wool. And it is mentioned that the mountains will move over the earth while in the form of mountains, like dust.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿As for him whose scales are heavy﴾

He says: as for him whose good deeds' scales are heavy. By "scales" (mawazin) is meant the weighing. The Arabs say: "For you I have a dirham by the measure of your dirham, and the weight of your dirham," and they say: "My house is by the measure of your house and the weight of your house," meaning: opposite your house. The poet said:

Indeed I was before meeting you a man of firmness; ... for every opponent I have his measure

By "for every opponent his measure" he means his speech, and that which overturns his argument. Mujahid used to say: it is not a literal scale; it is only a figure of speech.

* Abu Kurayb related to us with this, saying: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning ﴿he will be in a pleasing life﴾: he says, in a life which he is pleased with, in Paradise.

As:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿he will be in a pleasing life﴾: meaning, in Paradise.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And as for him whose scales are light, his mother will be the Abyss﴾

He says: and as for him whose good deeds' scales are light, his refuge and dwelling is the Abyss (al-Hawiyah), into which he will fall headlong in Hell.

Ahl al-ta'wil said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿And as for him whose scales are light, his mother will be the Abyss﴾: it is the Fire, it is their refuge.

* Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿his mother will be the Abyss﴾: he said: his destination is the Fire, it is the Abyss. Qatadah said: it is an Arabic expression; when a man fell into a severe matter, he would say: "his mother has fallen (hawat ummuh)."

* Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Ash'ath ibn Abd Allah al-A'má, who said: when a believer dies, his soul is taken to the souls of the believers, and they say: "Give rest to your brother, for he was in the distress of the world." He said: and they ask him, "What has become of so-and-so?" He says: "He died." Or: "Has he not come to you?" They say: "He has been taken to his mother, the Abyss."

* Isma'il ibn Sayf al-Ijli related to me, saying: Ali ibn Musahir related to us, saying: Isma'il related to us, from Abu Salih, concerning His saying ﴿his mother will be the Abyss﴾: he said: they will be made to fall into the Fire upon their heads.

* Ibn Sayf related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Sawwar related to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿his mother will be the Abyss﴾: he said: he falls into the Fire upon his head.

* Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿his mother will be the Abyss﴾: he said: the Abyss is the Fire; it is his mother and his refuge to which he returns and in which he takes shelter, and he recited: ﴿and their refuge is the Fire﴾.

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning ﴿his mother will be the Abyss﴾: he said: it is like her, and He made the Fire his mother only because it became his refuge, just as a mother shelters her son; so, since he has no refuge other than it, He made it, in that position, like a mother to him.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And what will make you know what it is?﴾

He, may His majesty be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): And what will make you aware, O Muhammad, of what the Abyss is? Then He explained what it is, saying: ﴿A Fire blazing fiercely﴾, meaning by "blazing" (hamiyah): that which has been heated by the fuel placed upon it.
